summary: Oscillatory autoscale feedback causing dedicated GPU shortfall and noisy-tenant isolation issues
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 09:10 UTC, NarrativeAI observed a stepwise degradation in throughput on their dedicated GPU pool. The platform autoscaler repeatedly scaled up and then rapidly down (oscillation) resulting in temporary GPU allocation shortfalls, elevated p99 latency, and an increase in 5xx responses for batched requests. The behavior correlates with a bursty set of short-lived streams from one tenant in the same pool that create slot fragmentation and cause prefetched KV cache thrash.

Impact: Customer experienced 20-40% reduction in sustained throughput for their pinned routes, p99 generation latency rose from ~220ms to ~1.6s during oscillation windows, and several requests returned 503/504 while autoscaler rebalanced. This affected production traffic for NarrativeAI between 09:10–11:45 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer runs large number of short inference streams (many < 2s) concurrently against gpt-medium-8b on dedicated pool; 2) Streams create fragmented small batches that prevent efficient batching; 3) Autoscaler observes ephemeral queue spikes and scales up; 4) Short bursts finish quickly, autoscaler scales down before warmed replicas can amortize prefetch cost; 5) Repeated cycles cause prefetch eviction and GPU warmup penalties, causing throughput collapse.

Notes: We could reproduce on an internal staging dedicated pool by orchestrating many short streams (see runbook below).
observed_behavior:
- Repeated autoscaler scale-up/scale-down events every 3–7 minutes.
- GPU allocation flapping: nodes attached/detached visible in allocation logs.
- High prefetch eviction rate and KV cache misses correlated with warmup tails.
- Elevated request 503/504 for pinned routes during downscales.
- Scheduler logs show slot fragmentation and frequent small-batch affinity changes.
expected_behavior: Stable autoscaler behavior with hysteresis preventing oscillation for short-lived bursts; sustained replicas sufficient for warm cache and stable batching; no 5xx spike during normal bursty traffic patterns.

metrics:
Key metrics observed during incident: 
- p99 latency (gpt-medium-8b, pinned route): baseline 220ms -> peak 1.6s
- sustained throughput: baseline 450 reqs/s -> observed 270 reqs/s (30% drop)
- autoscaler scale events: ~12 up/down cycles in 2 hours window
- KV cache hit rate: baseline 87% -> observed 42%
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: autoscaler reacting to short spikes without sufficient stabilization window combined with noisy tenant producing many short streams.

What we checked: 
- Autoscaler logs (timestamps show scaling decisions triggered by short-lived queue length increases).
- Prefetcher metrics: high eviction rate and increased warmup time.
- Scheduler allocation traces: slot fragmentation and preemption events from tenant X-tenant-77.
- Isolation controls: tenant rate limits were not configured for this pool.

Findings: 
- Autoscaler configured with default cooldown (60s) and minimal replicas set to 1; this allowed rapid downscales between bursts.
- Noisy tenant (internal identifier: X-tenant-77) generated thousands of sub-2s streams that prevented batch formation and inflated instantaneous queue length metrics.
- Prefetch eviction combined with aggressive downscaling produced repeated warmup penalties that the autoscaler misinterpreted as capacity over-provisioning.

Customer (NarrativeAI - Alex Ruiz) 2026-03-12 10:18 UTC: Confirmed they saw increased p99 and occasional 503s. They can throttle background short streams for 30 minutes on request.

SRE (Ravi Patel) 2026-03-12 10:45 UTC: Observed autoscaler logs showing repeated scale-downs ~90s after scale-up. Increasing stabilization window is a low-risk mitigation. Preparing runbook steps to reproduce on staging.

Platform Eng (Lena Ortiz) 2026-03-12 11:20 UTC: Noted the prefetched KV size increased ~3x for this customer; prefetched leases were being evicted at high rates. Suggested increasing min_replicas to 2 for pipeline-stability.
Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-12 11:35 UTC: Applied temporary mitigation per SRE suggestions: bumped autoscaler cooldown to 300s for pool and set min_replicas=2. Monitoring for 45 minutes.
Customer (Alex Ruiz) 2026-03-12 12:10 UTC: Reports throughputs returned to expected levels and p99 dropped back to ~260ms. Appreciative of quick mitigation.
resolution:
Mitigation applied (2026-03-12 11:35 UTC):
- Increased autoscaler stabilization window (cooldown) from 60s -> 300s for the affected dedicated pool.
- Raised min_replicas from 1 -> 2 to ensure warm cache retention.
- Applied per-tenant soft rate limit to noisy tenant X-tenant-77 to reduce stream fanout.

Result: Within 25–45 minutes, KV hit-rate recovered to ~80%, p99 returned to ~250–300ms, and 503s dropped to zero for customer routes.

Permanent follow-up actions assigned below.
follow_up_tasks: TASK-1: Update autoscaler default hysteresis for dedicated pools to use workload-aware cooldowns (owner: autoscale team, due: 2026-03-19).
TASK-2: Implement tenant-level short-stream detection and automated soft-rate-limits (owner: scheduler team, due: 2026-04-02).
TASK-3: Add prefetcher eviction alerting and dashboard panel (owner: runtime team, due: 2026-03-20).
TASK-4: Run fairness scheduler experiment from PR #3221 on canary pools and evaluate impact (owner: platform-eng, due: 2026-03-26).
